name: Right-wing antiglobalism
summary: Right-wing antiglobalism opposes "globalism", meaning free-trade economics, supranational bodies such as the UN, EU and WTO, open migration and the cultural liberalism it attaches to them, in defence of national sovereignty, borders, domestic industry and traditional culture. It frames a transnational elite as acting against ordinary citizens, and in some strands extends this to conspiracy theories about a New World Order, which critics say carry antisemitic tropes. It is mostly a thin, reactive position, so economic and social answers beyond trade, sovereignty and identity vary by strand.
scope: Mainstream contemporary antiglobalist right in the United States and Europe, as set out in the Wikipedia account and exemplified by Trump's 2018 and 2019 UN speeches and Buchanan's The Great Betrayal. Includes the Christian-right and John Birch Society lineage where documented. Excludes left-wing antiglobalism and the anti-globalization movement of the Global South, and treats conspiratorial extremes (QAnon, explicit antisemitic claims) as fringe unless stated. Many non-trade answers are inferences and marked low.

sources.usedFor: The claim that elites, the EU and UN promote mass migration, and its uptake by Orban, Le Pen and Zemmour.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Antiglobalists mostly frame the issue around borders and sovereignty; healthcare splits Christian-right and fiscal-conservative strands from welfare-minded populists. Inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Buchanan blames imports for depressed wages but answers with tariffs rather than wage floors, and the camp is divided on mandates. Inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Buchanan rejects free-market trade orthodoxy and wants the nation to steer its industry, though domestic markets are not the target. Inferred from the protectionist stance.

public-ownership.rationale: Strands defend national industry but through tariffs and private firms, and the Christian right opposes socialism; nationalisation is not a stated aim.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Buchanan attacks capital that moves abroad, yet the camp includes tax-cutting Republicans; no shared line on rates.

unions-good.rationale: Buchanan speaks for manufacturing workers hurt by trade but the right-wing camp is split on organised labor. Inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: The Birch Society and Christian-right lineage treat property rights as bedrock against collectivism, though documentation here is indirect.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Antiglobalists attack multinationals that offshore jobs but oppose regulation as a global-governance tool; adherents split.

cut-welfare.rationale: No shared stance: Birch-style conservatives favour cuts, populist nationalists defend benefits for citizens. Inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: Socialist-style ownership schemes fall under what the camp labels globalist or socialist, though it is rarely addressed.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Security hawkishness pulls toward yes, while distrust of unaccountable elites pulls toward no; not defined by the ideology.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The socially conservative, Christian-right wing leads the camp, which tends to oppose legalisation. Inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Hate-speech rules and the UN conventions behind them are cast as elite or global attempts to police dissent; the camp resists them.

strong-leader.rationale: Trump's speeches place the nation's will in a leader who defies the global establishment and gridlock; adherents favour such figures, though not unanimously.

state-harmful.rationale: The ideology is built around defending the nation-state's authority and sovereignty, so calling the state harmful contradicts it.

limit-guns.rationale: The American strands, Birch Society and Christian right, are gun-rights oriented and see disarmament schemes as global; European strands vary.

empower-police-military.rationale: Trump stresses record military funding and strength and defends border enforcement, so more resources for force is mainstream.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Social-conservative and religious stance of the camp opposes it. Inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Adherents prize sovereignty at the national level and sometimes the local one, but the statement sets local against national, and the camp is nationalist.

rehabilitation.rationale: Law-and-order rhetoric leans toward punishment, but the matter is peripheral to antiglobalism. Inferred.

traditional-family.rationale: Christian-right antiglobalists oppose UN conventions as attacks on the traditional family and parental rights, and champion that family model.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Globalism is said to bundle feminism and secular culture that undermine Christian values; mainstream adherents oppose, though some Western libertarian-leaning ones accept.

abortion-legal.rationale: Trump told the UN that every child born and unborn is a sacred gift and opposed international abortion funding; the Christian-right strand agrees.

more-religion-public.rationale: Trump stressed religious liberty and God-given dignity, and the Christian right sees secular global institutions as opposed to Christianity.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Seen as globalist and multicultural agenda; the camp stresses national identity over group redress. Inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Feminism and gender ideology are placed under the globalist umbrella by the Christian right, so the camp resists constructionist claims.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Defending national identity, traditions and culture against globalisation and multiculturalism is the defining theme in the Wikipedia account.

gradual-change.rationale: Conservative instincts coexist with a radical anti-establishment style that wants to break with the global order.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Trump says every nation has an absolute right to protect its borders and calls illegal migration harmful; the camp ties globalisation to mass migration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Trump rejects global governance, saying the US will always choose independence over it; the UN, EU and WTO are cast as threats.

free-trade.rationale: Buchanan offers a root-and-branch rejection of free trade and Trump demands trade that is fair and reciprocal.

nation-first.rationale: The 2018 UN speech rejects the ideology of globalism and embraces the doctrine of patriotism, putting national interest ahead of global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Trump's UN speeches stress sovereignty and non-interference; intervention for human rights is associated with global governance, though hawks exist.

open-borders.rationale: Trump criticises activists who demand erasure of national borders and claims the right to protect them.

limit-growth.rationale: The camp rejects Agenda 2030 and environmental limits as globalist; Trump's UN speech promotes expanded energy production and exports.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The Wikipedia account lists the SDGs and environmentalism among globalist projects and the camp opposes climate agreements.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: No documented shared view; the camp is suspicious of tech elites in some strands and fond of industrial growth in others.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Pro-energy-production stance and national self-sufficiency suggest support, but nuclear is not discussed in the sources. Inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: Patriotic and law-abiding rhetoric dominates in the sources, although some militias and conspiracists accept it. Inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: Distrust of globalist technocrats and expert-led bodies like the WHO and UN is central, as in the camp's COVID-19 and Agenda 2030 views.

central-planning.rationale: The camp treats socialism and global planning as parts of globalism and defends national industry through protection, not planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Socialist models of ownership sit under the globalist umbrella for the Christian right; not directly addressed.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not an issue the sources link to the ideology; no shared view.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Family and property conservatism disfavour estate taxes, though not documented here. Inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Welfare expansion is not part of the agenda and the Christian right and Birch strand oppose it. Inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Buchanan credits tariffs with building American industry and the Wikipedia account lists protection of domestic industries as a core economic stance.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Buchanan's economic nationalism backs industrial protection, but direction of investment is not stated and market conservatives dissent.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Wikipedia says supporters seek to protect small businesses and domestic producers from foreign competition; the ideal is not stated in those terms.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A socialist abolition of wage labor is the opposite of the camp's property-defending, anti-socialist outlook.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Birch Society tradition opposed the Federal Reserve, but not all adherents share this; stance not documented in the sources used.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not a feature of the documented camp, and it is hostile to socialist-style planning. Inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Trump rejects it implicitly by invoking democracy and sovereign nations; the camp frames itself as defending self-government.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The question is peripheral; some traditionalists are sympathetic but the camp is mostly republican in the US.

democracy-best.rationale: Trump says if you want democracy, hold on to your sovereignty, tying national self-rule to democracy, though many distrust voters' supposed manipulation.

direct-votes.rationale: Referendums such as Brexit appeal to the camp, but the position isn't central. Inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils as the basis of power is a socialist model the camp opposes.

right-to-secede.rationale: The camp is nation-centred, wary of splitting the nation, though anti-federal strands and Brexit-style exit are sympathetic.

natural-rulers.rationale: Not a documented position of this camp; populist anti-elitism runs against it.

political-violence-never.rationale: Mainstream adherents reject violence while conspiratorial fringes do not; contested.

war-builds-character.rationale: Trump frames strength as peace through strength rather than war as purifying. Inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Christian right sees secular influences as part of globalism and wants Christian values in public life.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Christian-right strands want scriptural influence, but most nationalists do not call for laws from scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Defence and justice belong to sovereign nations; Trump condemns surrendering authority to unaccountable bodies.

military-superiority.rationale: Trump says the US military will be more powerful than ever and stresses record defense funding.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Wikipedia calls the stance ethno-nationalist, but the mainstream camp speaks of civic patriotism; split.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Marxist class conflict is opposed; the camp stresses nation and culture and treats socialism as globalist.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Equality of outcomes is bound up with socialism and feminism that the camp counts as globalist.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Seen as part of UN-driven agendas by the Christian right; not stated directly.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The camp opposes global redistribution and guilt-based agendas; Trump's UN stance is that aid go only to friends.

civilizational-union.rationale: Union across nations is read as global governance; Trump wants independence among sovereign states.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Trump's America First tone treats national self-interest as legitimate, though individual-level ethics isn't addressed.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Communitarian-nationalist pull is offset by Birch-style individual-rights tradition; split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmentalism sits under the globalist umbrella; the camp resists it, although conservationists exist.

limit-population.rationale: Population control is part of UN agendas that the Christian right opposes. Inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Buchanan celebrates industrial power built under tariffs and mourns lost manufacturing; the camp defends industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Distrust of globalist technocratic projects makes disruptive acceleration unattractive. Inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Religious conservatives dominate the camp and distrust it. Inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The camp opposes unaccountable technocratic governance, and AI rule would mean more of it.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: No shared stance; security hawks and anti-state libertarians differ.

restore-past-order.rationale: Buchanan wants to restore the pre-New Deal economy and the camp seeks to restore lost national tradition.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Trump speeches present pragmatism, but the camp is also strongly ideological about globalism.

direct-action.rationale: Mainstream adherents work through elections and states, though protest movements occur.

means-match-ends.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no defined position.

return-to-foraging.rationale: A defender of industry and national production would reject abandoning civilization.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of any right-wing outlook; the camp protects industrial employment.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Communist distribution is opposed as socialism, which the camp groups with globalism.

production-for-use.rationale: Anti-profit production is a socialist idea; the camp mostly defends private enterprise within the nation.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Exploitation theory of profit is Marxist and rejected, even though Buchanan attacks capital moving jobs abroad.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: A Marxist revolutionary doctrine the camp opposes.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The camp does not hold the Leninist thesis; it blames globalists and internationalism, not capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: Birch-style libertarian-leaning members agree, populist nationalists accept taxes; split.

harm-principle.rationale: Not a stated concern and social conservatives would add moral limits; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The camp stresses national and family groups, though Birch tradition emphasises individual liberty.

conscription.rationale: Strong defence posture is shared but conscription is not discussed in the sources.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Trump ties democracy to sovereignty, favouring voting and national self-rule. Inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Trump's business image fits, yet the camp is not defined by the idea.

positive-liberty.rationale: The camp emphasises sovereignty and negative liberty from global control, rather than material enabling. Inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: The camp views globalist media and academic elites as powerful and hostile, as in conspiracies about cabals.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Fringe ethno-nationalists affirm it, mainstream adherents do not discuss; split.

organic-representation.rationale: Not documented; populists favour direct popular expression over corporatist bodies.

total-state.rationale: Opposition to a state directing all life fits with defending sovereignty and rejecting statist socialism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Buchanan's new nationalism and Trump's patriotism call for renewing the nation after a perceived betrayal, though decadence language varies.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Trump emphasises sovereignty and non-interference in others' affairs, and the camp is wary of foreign entanglements.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal bonds are not part of the program.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is unconnected to and incompatible with this ideology.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Adherents distrust academia, but they claim truth against elite narratives rather than endorsing relativism.

universal-morality.rationale: Trump invokes God-given dignity and Christian-right moral truth, though the nationalist wing stresses particular cultures.

single-common-good.rationale: No stated view; the camp pits people against elites but does not specify.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Trump and Milei are pro-Israel, though the antisemitic strand opposes; contested among adherents.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No defined view, and the camp is restrictionist about citizenship.

school-vouchers.rationale: Christian-right and parental-rights stances favour school choice, though not documented in the sources.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Buchanan objects to trade deficits rather than fiscal ones, and the camp is split.

economic-freedom.rationale: Buchanan departs from free-market orthodoxy while Birch-style conservatives accept it; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Not documented and the camp uses law and enforcement.

national-self-determination.rationale: Trump says sovereign nations should govern themselves and honour each other's sovereignty, the core of the ideology.

force-without-un.rationale: Trump rejects global governance and the primacy of international bodies over US choices, implying freedom to act without UN approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Christian right and Trump's religious appeals favour faith; reason alone is not the guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Trump says foreign aid goes only to friends and the camp links migration with strain on citizens; welfare chauvinism is common in the populist right.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Conservative norms support work requirements, though not documented in the sources used.

class-collaboration.rationale: The camp prefers national solidarity to class struggle, though Buchanan speaks for workers against capital.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The camp's core is preserving national tradition and culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Common front among dominated countries is a left-antiglobalist idea; the right frames nations as independent.

workers-nation.rationale: The camp wants workers organised in the national interest, as in Buchanan's new nationalism, not an international class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Buchanan blames women entering the workforce for decline, and the Christian right defends traditional roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Not a documented position; market conservatives oppose.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The mainstream camp does not advocate legal segregation, even if ethno-nationalist fringes do.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Marxist view of the state is opposed; the camp holds the nation-state as legitimate.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Trump pledged to export abundant oil, clean coal and natural gas, and the camp rejects climate agendas.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Defence of national culture implies immigrants conform, though some strands want less immigration instead.

elite-replacement.rationale: Camus and the replacement theory claim elites, the EU and UN promote mass immigration; mainstream antiglobalists adopt versions, though not all.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; populists often prefer majoritarian systems. Inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Trump explicitly rejects imposing the US system on others and stresses each nation's own path.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The camp lists feminism as globalist and denies the claim.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The camp casts a globalist elite as hostile to the people; this elite-versus-nation framing is central.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not an established position, and the religious right opposes eugenics. Inferred.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Trump rejects international accountability bodies like the ICC, and the camp backs the military and police.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Birch heritage says yes while populist nationalists prefer an active state in trade; split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Mainstream adherents do not advocate it though ethno-nationalist fringes do.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Christian right assumes human dignity, but ethno-nationalist strands conflict; contested.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The claim is a left-antiglobalist one; the camp rejects it as guilt-based.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Common law for all citizens fits national uniformity, but the issue is peripheral.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Trump supports religious liberty for all; not a stated aim.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu-nationalist issue outside this camp.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Christian right prefers religious expression in schools. Inferred.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine; the camp is anti-socialist and treats socialism as part of globalism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Trump says "we will never surrender sovereignty to unelected, unaccountable bureaucracy", an argument based on popular consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Buchanan decries record trade deficits and Trump demands reciprocal trade; surpluses are favoured.

population-transfer.rationale: Not a mainstream stance though ethno-nationalist fringes agree.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Libertarian-leaning members say yes, while hawks reject it; split.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Not stated; mixed with a protectionist suspicion of competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Seeing itself as outsiders opposed by elites, the camp resists party bans.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Trump's talk of avoiding domination by global bodies echoes it, but it isn't framed philosophically.

separated-powers.rationale: Trump and Birch-style constitutionalists defend constitutional checks, though not directly documented.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Leninist doctrine the camp rejects.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Not defined by it; the camp speaks for workers and citizens rather than the poor as such.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British Thatcherite policy, not an antiglobalist position.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; fiscal conservatives yes, populists no.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The sources give no stance on poverty and population, and adherents have no common line.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The camp says globalisation and multiculturalism dilute national culture and identity, so diversity erodes cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not part of the camp's program; it defends elected sovereign institutions.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Strong-state tendencies are offset by constitutionalist distrust of state power; split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing is not documented; market conservatives oppose and the camp defends enterprise within the nation.

party-controls-media.rationale: The camp denounces elite control of media and favours free speech against it.

party-commands-army.rationale: Party control of the army is a communist doctrine.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Restrictive immigration views extend to citizenship, though not detailed in sources.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Anti-establishment populists dislike party discipline. Inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Wikipedia lists the EU among organisations the camp opposes, and Trump says sovereignty must not be surrendered.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Executive command of the military is a constitutional-design question the sources do not take up.

clerical-rule.rationale: Christian-right influence does not extend to rule by clerics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The camp is patriotic and supports its own nation in war.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Religious conservatives would, free-speech conservatives would not; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not a topic in the sources, and adherents' views follow their own national setting.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials is not discussed in the sources and no shared position is documented.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Trump says other countries should pay more for their defence and is cool to entanglements, but he keeps alliances; contested.

people-in-arms.rationale: American militia strands endorse armed citizenry, but the camp backs a strong military; split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Heartland, traditional values and agrarian imagery suit the camp, though not documented.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The sources do not address reunification of divided nations; no shared position is documented.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The camp is anti-elitist and sees educated globalist elites as removed from ordinary citizens.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The camp defends its own culture against others and denies equal fit, though it does not rank cultures formally.

death-penalty.rationale: Law-and-order conservatives mostly support it, though not documented here.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The Christian right opposes UN-driven gender equality and sex education as eroding parental rights.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Christian-right strands support it while secular nationalists do not; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Christian-right social conservatism favours restrictions, though not documented.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The American strand supports birthright citizenship restrictions; European ones use descent; split.

minority-language-support.rationale: Preserving a single national culture pulls against it. Inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Religious liberty is central for Christians, but exemptions for minorities are not.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Defending tradition favours custom over eccentricity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Trump ties aid to loyalty to the US; cancelling debts is a left-antiglobalist demand.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution-rewriting procedure is not addressed by the sources, so no position can be inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The camp talks of freedom and sovereignty, though it favours strong authority.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Trump says aid goes only to those who respect the US, and the camp rejects obligations to global redistribution.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Sovereignty emphasis and strong defence favour independent capability, though not stated for nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: How a head of state is chosen is not discussed in the sources and adherents differ by country.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Distrust of unaccountable technocrats and the Birch anti-Fed tradition oppose independence.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property is held as a right and fundamental, not conditional.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not a concern of this camp.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental global rules are opposed; the camp rejects the principle as a vehicle for global governance.

collective-defense.rationale: Trump demands allies pay more and sceptically treats alliances; contested.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Trump's UN speech defends sovereignty generally but the sources say nothing on annexed territory.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Christian right defends church independence.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The sources do not discuss ceremonial heads of state, and a partisan US president is typical here.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Not addressed; sovereignty implies unity, but self-rule favours exit.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Not addressed; nationalist unity pulls against it.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Divine descent of rulers is not part of the creed.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; conservative instinct favours innate nature, but unspoken.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Trump frames sovereignty as the nation's, accountable to citizens, not rulers above law.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is not mentioned in any source on the ideology, so it has no defined view.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Mixed-constitution theory is not part of this ideology's documented sources.

leader-cult.rationale: Trump's political style invites personality displays but the ideology does not require them.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; some men's-rights strands overlap.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist thesis that the camp rejects.

land-redistribution.rationale: Opposed to confiscation as property conservatives and anti-socialists.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; restrictionist camp opposes migration compacts.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Trump stresses respect for borders and sovereignty; Orbán-style views differ; split.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Trump endorses religious liberty for all.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not a Western nationalist stance and opposed as a foreign religious law.

common-currency.rationale: The EU and global bodies are opposed, so an international currency is rejected.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Cultural separatism for minorities cuts against national culture. Inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy of emigration versus local rights is not addressed by the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The camp attributes decline to elite ideas and policy, not impersonal materialism. Inferred.

ban-cartels.rationale: Buchanan's attacks on big multinationals suggest sympathy, but market conservatives oppose.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; populists and Birch anti-bailout tradition lean yes.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Distrust of liberal courts and institutions fits, though not directly documented.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas are linked to UN women's conventions and feminism that the camp opposes.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Buchanan urges national industrial self-reliance and protection, but a closed bloc is stronger than he states.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Trump rejects binding international bodies and demands bilateral reciprocity instead.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Foco theory is Marxist-Guevarist and unrelated.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Titles and hereditary privilege are not discussed in the sources, so no stance is inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Teaching national culture and heritage fits the camp's cultural defence.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The camp opposes global governance but not necessarily tutelage; not addressed.

patriotic-education.rationale: Trump says if you want freedom, take pride in your country; patriotism is the central value.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial redress is treated as part of the multicultural global agenda the camp opposes.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not documented, though Birch-style monetary critics might back it.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources do not discuss capitalism's crises; adherents are not defined by a view on this.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; the camp favours withdrawal from foreign entanglements.

delink-world-market.rationale: Buchanan wants protection but not delinking; a left-antiglobalist idea, split.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory the camp does not hold.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian strands agree and populist strands do not; split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: American constitutionalist heritage favours it, though not documented.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: A left-antiglobalist claim; the camp is sceptical of redress.

minority-veto.rationale: Not documented and conflicts with majority populism.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Constitutionalist heritage and distrust of unaccountable elites imply it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The camp defends national legislatures against global bodies, but not specifically parliamentary supremacy; Brexit suggests yes.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal welfare is not covered by the sources on this ideology, so no position is documented.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use is not covered by the sources on this ideology, so no position is documented.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Elite obligation is not a documented theme; the camp mostly attacks elites rather than urging duties.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Activist movement in politics; withdrawal contradicts it.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The camp blames elite media but not as pacifier of order; split.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony theory is Gramscian; not addressed.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Buchanan says the US loses jobs to imports rather than the Marxist-dependency claim of extraction from poor countries.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nativism implies it; not documented explicitly.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party independence is a question of the left and does not apply to this ideology.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Trump says aid goes only to those who respect the US, and national self-reliance matches the camp's sovereignty emphasis.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is not documented as part of the strand; Orban-style views differ from American ones.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The camp is hostile to this left-leaning value, and critics tie its conspiracy theories to fascist antecedents.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anti-socialist stance leads to equating the two, though not documented.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not an ideological position of the camp.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Defence of national heritage and tradition extends to monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Buchanan and the Christian right favour a traditional male role, but this is a contested modern issue.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources are silent on domestic violence policy, though men's-rights themes overlap with some adherents.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Trump urges every nation to pursue its own path and rejects imposing a global model.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Not addressed; the camp is pro-military, but guardianship is not documented.

paid-care-work.rationale: Buchanan blames working women for decline and the camp favours the traditional household.

missingStatements.text: Migration should be governed by each nation's own laws, not by international agreements or bodies.
missingStatements.rationale: Trump said migration should not be governed by an international body unaccountable to citizens and refused the Global Compact on Migration.

missingStatements.text: Countries should not accept the jurisdiction of international courts over their own citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: Trump declared the ICC has no jurisdiction, legitimacy or authority over America, a central sovereignty claim.

missingStatements.text: Government should favor domestic workers and producers over cheaper imports, even at higher prices.
missingStatements.rationale: Buchanan defends protection for domestic manufacturing and jobs against cheaper imports as the core of his new nationalism.

notes: Strands diverge: Birch and Christian-right antiglobalists add anti-UN, anti-feminist and eschatological themes; Buchanan-style economic nationalists focus on trade; Orbán and Le Pen-style strands add migration and replacement claims. The term globalist is contested and critics link it to antisemitic conspiracy theories.
